SearchAliases: a painted cake cannot satisfy hunger

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A painted cake is repeatedly named as something that cannot feed: the records apply that bodily limit to words, talk, blows, and shouts that likewise fail to satisfy hunger.
EvidenceBody: Literally a cake drawn or painted rather than edible. Chan records make it a stock verdict by completing the image: “a painted cake cannot fill hunger” . In the Xiangyan case, after he cannot answer Guishan's question and searches all the writings he has read for a reply, he sighs, “a painted cake cannot fill hunger” ; the record then has him burn those writings. Dahui's verse pairs it with another ineffective likeness: “how could a shimmering mirage ever stop thirst? When could a painted cake fill hunger?” . The verdict extends beyond writings. One discourse says “discussing the obscure and speaking of the marvelous is like using a painted cake to fill hunger” ; another asks whether wielding the staff and shouting differs from filling hunger with a painted cake . A verse explicitly places it beside “speaking of food never makes one full” . Thus the object keeps its literal non-feeding property while the corpus repeatedly applies it to quoted words, explanations, stock gestures, and other substitutes that it says do not fill hunger.
